title: State Newton's first law of motion

hook.scenario: Agar table par ek book rakhi hai, toh woh saalo saal wahin rakhi rahegi jab tak koi usko haath na lagaye. Aur agar koi spacecraft space mein chal raha hai, toh uska engine band hone par bhi woh hamesha chalta rahega.
hook.question: Objects apni current state mein hi rehna kyun chahte hain?

mental_model.intuition: Cheezein aalsi (lazy) hoti hain. Woh jo kar rahi hoti hain, wahi karte rehna chahti hain, jab tak koi force unhe disturb na kare.
mental_model.description: Newton ka First Law kehta hai ki har object ek natural laziness dikhata hai. Ruka hua object ruka rehna chahta hai, aur chalne wala object constant speed aur ek seedhi line mein chalte rehna chahta hai, jab tak koi external unbalanced force aakar uski state ko badal na de.

explanation:
Newton's First Law of Motion classical physics ka sabse fundamental rule hai. Ise Law of Inertia bhi kaha jata hai. Yeh law simple shabdon mein kehta hai: "An object remains in a state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change that state by an applied force." Is statement mein do cases aate hain jo dhyaan se samajhne wale hain.

Pehla case un cheezon ke liye hai jo rest par hain. Jaise tumhari table par rakha hua coffee mug. Woh apne aap chalna shuru nahi karega. Us par gravity neeche lag rahi hai, aur table ka normal force upar. Yeh dono forces balanced hain, isliye net force zero hai. Jab tak tum us mug par push ya pull (unbalanced force) nahi lagaoge, woh wahi rakha rahega.

Doosra case thoda counter-intuitive hai—un objects ke bare mein jo motion mein hain. Zameen par chalne wali gaadi ya ball kuch der baad ruk jaati hai. Humein lagta hai ki motion ko maintain karne ke liye force chahiye. Lekin asal mein, ball isliye rukti hai kyunki friction aur air resistance jaise invisible forces uspar lag rahe hote hain. Deep space mein jahan friction zero hota hai, agar tum kisi cheez ko dhakka de kar chhod do, toh woh hamesha ke liye ek straight line mein constant speed se chalti rahegi.

Iska basic matlab yeh hai ki kisi bhi force ki zaroorat kisi cheez ko chalane ke liye nahi, balki uski movement ya direction ko *change* karne ke liye hoti hai. Agar state of motion change nahi ho rahi, toh pakka koi unbalanced force nahi lag raha.

key_points.title: Objects at Rest
key_points.detail: An object at rest stays at rest completely unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.

key_points.title: Objects in Motion
key_points.detail: An object in uniform motion stays in uniform straight-line motion indefinitely unless an unbalanced force is applied.

worked_example.problem: A spacecraft is drifting in deep space (where there is no gravity and no friction) at a constant velocity of 500 m/s. What is the net force required to keep it moving at this exact speed?

steps.narration: Deep space mein koi friction nahi hai. Spacecraft ki velocity constant hai.
Newton's first law ke mutabiq, constant velocity maintain karne ke liye koi net force nahi chahiye hota.

worked_example.answer: The net force required is 0 N.

worked_example.problem: A heavy box rests on a horizontal floor. The downward force of gravity on the box is 50 N. Why does the box remain at rest, and what force opposes gravity?

steps.narration: Box rest par hai, iska matlab net force zero hona chahiye.
Downward gravity ko balance karne ke liye floor ki taraf se upward normal force lagta hai.

worked_example.answer: The box remains at rest because the net force is zero. The floor exerts an upward normal force of 50 N.

common_mistakes.title: Believing a continuous force is needed for continuous motion
common_mistakes.explanation: Humein lagta hai ki engine lagatar chalna chahiye gaadi ko chalane ke liye. Gaadi ko force sirf road ke friction ko cancel karne ke liye chahiye hota hai, na ki constant speed maintain karne ke khud ke liye.

recall_questions.q: What is the alternative name for Newton's first law of motion?
Why does a rolling ball eventually stop?
recall_questions.answer: Due to the unbalanced force of friction acting on it.

recall_questions.q: What happens to a moving object in the complete absence of any net force?
recall_questions.answer: It will continue to move in a straight line with uniform velocity forever.

oa_questions.question: State Newton's first law of motion.
oa_questions.answer: An object continues to be in a state of rest or of uniform motion along a straight line unless acted upon by an unbalanced external force.
oa_questions.approach: Write the exact standard statement avoiding changes to words like 'unbalanced' or 'uniform motion'.

oa_questions.question: Why is it advised to tie any luggage kept on the roof of a bus with a rope?
oa_questions.answer: To prevent it from falling off due to inertia of rest or motion when the bus suddenly starts or stops.
oa_questions.approach: Use the concept of Newton's first law.
